requirements.label: physics
requirements.title: Courses in Physics
requirements.sourceText: PHY 131 - Classical Physics I 3 credits (See Note 1); PHY 133 - Classical Physics Laboratory I 1 credit (See Note 1); PHY 132 - Classical Physics II 3 credits (See Note 1); PHY 134 - Classical Physics Laboratory II 1 credit (See Note 1); PHY 251 - Modern Physics 3 credits; PHY 252 - Modern Physics Laboratory 1 credit; PHY 277 - Computation for Physics and Astronomy 3 credits; PHY 300 - Waves and Optics 4 credits; PHY 301 - Electromagnetic Theory I 3 credits; PHY 303 - Mechanics 3 credits; PHY 306 - Thermodynamics, Kinetic Theory, and Statistical Mechanics 3 credits; PHY 308 - Quantum Physics 3 credits; PHY 335 - Electronics and Instrumentation Laboratory 3 credits; PHY 445 - Senior Laboratory 3 credits

requirements.label: calculus
requirements.title: Calculus sequence (one of the following)
requirements.sourceText: One of the following sequences: MAT 125 - Calculus A; MAT 126 - Calculus B; MAT 127 - Calculus C; OR MAT 131 - Calculus I; MAT 132 - Calculus II; OR MAT 141 - Honors Calculus I; MAT 142 - Honors Calculus II; OR MAT 171 - Accelerated Single Variable Calculus; OR AMS 151 - Applied Calculus I; AMS 161 - Applied Calculus II. Note: Equivalency for MAT courses achieved on the Mathematics Placement Examination is accepted as fulfillment of the corresponding requirements, as indicated in the Course Descriptions section of this Bulletin.

requirements.label: placement-math
requirements.title: Placement-dependent MAT 123

rule.manualCheck: Check the math placement result. If the student did not place into MAT 125 or MAT 131, MAT 123 (or MAT 119 and MAT 123) is required.
rule.text: If students do not place into MAT 125 or MAT 131 on the basis of the math placement examination, MAT 123 (or MAT 119 /MAT 123) is a required course for the major.
rule.reason: Requirement depends on the placement examination result, which is not on a transcript.

requirements.sourceText: If students do not place into MAT 125 or MAT 131 on the basis of the math placement examination, MAT 123 (or MAT 119 /MAT 123) is a required course for the major.

requirements.label: math-multivariable
requirements.title: Multivariable calculus (one of the following)
requirements.sourceText: One of the following: MAT 203 - Calculus III with Applications 4 credits; OR AMS 261 - Applied Calculus III 4 credits; OR MAT 307 - Multivariable Calculus with Linear Algebra 4 credits

requirements.label: math-diffeq
requirements.title: Differential equations (one of the following)
requirements.sourceText: One of the following: MAT 303 - Calculus IV with Applications 4 credits; OR AMS 361 - Applied Calculus IV: Differential Equations 4 credits; OR MAT 308 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra 4 credits

requirements.label: math-linear-algebra
requirements.title: Linear algebra (one of the following)
requirements.sourceText: One of the following: MAT 211 - Introduction to Linear Algebra 3 credits; OR AMS 210 - Applied Linear Algebra 3 credits; OR MAT 307 - Multivariable Calculus with Linear Algebra 4 credits AND MAT 308 - Differential Equations with Linear Algebra 4 credits

requirements.label: related-fields
requirements.title: Courses in Related Fields (12 credits)

rule.manualCheck: The catalog also allows unlisted courses: many 200- and 300-level courses in ESE, ESM, GEO, MAR, MEC, BME and other listed areas, other 300-level courses noted after several entries, courses required by a minor, second major or master's program, and any course the Director of Undergraduate Studies approves. These cannot be checked from the listed codes alone.

requirements.sourceText: Twelve credits of physics-related courses that complement a Physics major's education are required. ... Additional related courses are listed below, but they are not exclusive. If another course is of interest and should qualify under the above goals, consult the undergraduate program director to see if it can be included.

requirements.label: writing
requirements.title: Upper-Division Writing Requirement

rule.manualCheck: Confirm the student completed a writing project within the major, approved by the supervisor and the undergraduate program director. Satisfaction is certified independently of the course grade and is best completed in the junior year.

requirements.sourceText: Students are certified as satisfying the upper-division writing requirement by registering for the 0-credit PHY 459 and completing a writing project within their major.

requirements.label: residency-300
requirements.title: Stony Brook residency for 300-level courses

rule.text: At least four courses numbered 300 or above must be taken at Stony Brook.
rule.reason: Course-count residency for upper-level courses is not expressible with the available residency policies, which take credit minimums.

requirements.sourceText: At least four courses numbered 300 or above must be taken at Stony Brook.

requirements.label: c-minus-allowance
requirements.title: C- allowance for lower-division courses

rule.text: All courses used to satisfy the major requirements must be completed with a grade of C or higher, except that a maximum of three courses at the 100- or 200-level may be completed with a grade of C-.
rule.reason: The grade minimum policy cannot express a cap on the number of C- grades allowed at the 100- or 200-level.

requirements.sourceText: All courses used to satisfy the major requirements must be completed with a grade of C or higher, except that a maximum of three courses at the 100- or 200-level may be completed with a grade of C-.

policies.sourceText: All courses used to satisfy the major requirements must be completed with a grade of C or higher, except that a maximum of three courses at the 100- or 200-level may be completed with a grade of C-.

with.text: Either PHY 125, PHY 126, PHY 127 with labs PHY 133 and PHY 134, or PHY 141/PHY 133 with PHY 142/PHY 134 (PHY 127 may be taken before PHY 126).
with.reason: The substitute is one of two alternative course sets, which cannot be expressed as a single substitution with the allowed nested rule types.

substitutions.sourceText: The sequence PHY 125, PHY 126, PHY 127 with labs PHY 133 and PHY 134 or PHY 141/PHY 133, PHY 142/PHY 134 may substitute for PHY 131/PHY 133, PHY 132/PHY 134. PHY 127 may be taken before PHY 126.

substitutions.condition: PHY/BME double majors who graduate with a BE in Biomedical Engineering
substitutions.sourceText: PHY/BME double majors who graduate with a BE in Biomedical Engineering may substitute BME 120 for PHY 277.

notes.text: All courses used to satisfy the major requirements must be completed with a grade of C or higher, except that a maximum of three courses at the 100- or 200-level may be completed with a grade of C-.
Completion of the major requires approximately 65 credits.
PHY/CSE double majors who graduate with a BS in Computer Science are exempt from PHY 277.

Physics Honors Program (not evaluated): to receive the BS in Physics with honors, a student must complete PHY 487 - Research (0-6 credits, at least 3 credits total), two other 400-level physics courses (three credits each, excluding PHY 475), and an overall GPA of at least 3.30 in all physics courses numbered 300 or higher.

Specialization in Optics (optional, not evaluated): PHY 302, PHY 452, at least three credits of PHY 487 (optics related), and one additional elective (PHY 405 or an approved course from another department). Listed on the official transcript.
The Physics Secondary Teacher Education Program is described under the Education and Teacher Certification entry in the alphabetical listings of Approved Majors, Minors, and Programs.

Students should consult with the department advisor to ensure that their plan for completing the Upper Division Writing Requirement is consistent with university graduation requirements for General Education. Students who wish to pursue graduate study in physics should choose a program similar to the Research Program example in the catalog (not evaluated).

The Introductory Physics Sequences are PHY 121/PHY 122 (for biological sciences and pre-medical/pre-health majors), PHY 131/PHY 133 with PHY 132/PHY 134, PHY 141/PHY 133 with PHY 142/PHY 134, and PHY 125, PHY 126, PHY 127 with PHY 133 and PHY 134. The two-semester sequences are for students prepared for a faster pace; PHY 141/142 is designed for the strongest physics and math preparation.
